messages:
Noelle G.: Hey team — employee submitted a ticket: spouse had ER visit last week and insurer denied the claim for 'not covered / member not on file'. They got a balance bill. Employee says spouse was added during open enrollment but last name change happened after. Need next steps.
Hector V.: Ask employee to upload enrollment confirmation and marriage certificate. We often see name mismatches causing the carrier to not match the dependent.
Noelle G.: They uploaded the enrollment confirmation email and the marriage cert. Member portal shows spouse on file but insurer's portal still has old last name.
Erin M.: Standard: File an enrollment data mismatch correction with the carrier and request retroactive effective date for dependent. Also request expedited adjudication for the denied claim.
Noelle G.: Can we issue a one-off temporary ID letter the clinic will accept? The employee is worried about collections.
Billing Ops: We can generate a manual coverage verification letter showing spouse added effective [MM/DD/YYYY]. Need last4 and DOB for the spouse.
Noelle G.: Sent last4 9876 and DOB 06/02/1990 for spouse. Member ID ends with R123.
benefits-bot: Automated: Typical carrier data-correction window is 7-14 business days; appeals/reprocessing after corrected enrollment: 14-45 days. Expedited clinical reviews may be 72 hours if marked urgent. See carrier guide: https://insurer.example/enrollment-fix
Erin M.: Template to carrier (paste into portal message/email):```Subject: Enrollment Data Correction - Dependent Name Mismatch Member: [EmployeeName], Member ID: [ID]Dependent: [SpouseName] DOB: [MM/DD/YYYY]Issue: Dependent enrolled via OE but carrier file shows old last name. Requested action: update dependent name to [NewLastName], retroactive effective date [MM/DD/YYYY], and reprocess denied claim #[claim#]. Attachments: enrollment confirmation screenshot, marriage certificate, EOB. Contact: benefits@redwood.com```
Hector V.: Provider-side: ask ER billing to hold collections and resubmit claim after reprocessing. Provider template:```Hello, Please hold any collection activity for patient [SpouseName] (last4 [9876]) while we resolve coverage enrollment. If claim previously denied, please re-submit claim #[orig_claim] once coverage is confirmed. Attachments: temp coverage letter. Please confirm holding collections and provide a resubmission confirmation number. Thank you. - People Ops```
Noelle G.: Sent the carrier message and the temp coverage verification PDF to the hospital billing (billing@eastside-er.org). Employee has been copied.
benefits-bot: Automated reminder: If carrier denies reprocessing after data fix, escalate to broker and consider external review. Document tracking ID: BEN-2026-912.
Erin M.: I've opened a broker escalation and asked for expedited matching (case #BR-5591). Broker requested a scanned marriage cert and enrollment ack — forwarded.
Hector V.: Important: ask carrier to reference the original claim number when reprocessing. That speeds matching.
Noelle G.: Hospital replied — they will hold collections and will resubmit after carrier confirms; provisional hold code set. They asked for expected timeline.
Erin M.: Tell them 7-14 business days for data correction, 14-45 days for reprocess. If they need proof now, provide the temp coverage letter and the enrollment screenshot.
Noelle G.: Forwarded timelines. Employee says collection agency called — told them to forward voicemail to benefits@redwood.com and we will flag collections team.
Billing Ops: Noted; we will freeze internal collection escalation while case is open.
Noelle G.: Carrier updated dependent name today and confirmed reprocessing. They provided resubmission ID 882-334. Forwarded to employee and hospital. Closing loop once EOB updates. :white_check_mark:
